title: Struct Members and Member Access
learningObjectives: Explain struct members and member access.
Trace member access and function behavior.
Recognize common design or access mistakes.
Create a small structured type with appropriate operations.

understand.concept: Members are fields or functions belonging to a type. The dot operator accesses a member through an object; arrow accesses a member through a pointer to an object.
understand.whyItMatters: Member access keeps related data and operations grouped.
understand.explain: Use dot for objects and -> for object pointers; ensure member names and types match.

examples.title: Dot operator
examples.explanation: Dot accesses a member through an object.

examples.title: Arrow through pointer
examples.explanation: Arrow is member access through a pointer.

examples.title: Change multiple fields
examples.explanation: Each field can be assigned independently.

examples.title: Member in condition
examples.explanation: A field can participate in a decision.

practise.guidedTask: Trace each Struct Members and Member Access example. Identify each object, member, access path and initialization value. Describe how the object state changes.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ program that models struct members and member access in a realistic scenario. Include appropriate initialization, operations, input validation where needed, and tests for typical and boundary values.
hints: Define the type before creating its objects.
Use dot for objects and arrow for pointers.
Keep fields private when enforcing invariants.
Test object creation and member operations.

questions.explanation: Arrow accesses members through a pointer.
Access names must refer to declared members.

questions.explanation: Fields can be part of expressions.
Dot on object, arrow on pointer.
